dedupe_keys.name: western central african republic ground and satellite damage assessment of villages 2013 to 2014 human rights watch

description: Human Rights Watch assessed 790 villages and towns in western Central African Republic on the ground and from satellite imagery for the period April 2013 to April 2014, and OCHA published the resulting geodatabase on the Humanitarian Data Exchange. It identified conflict-related building destruction in 125 villages, with more than 17,500 mostly residential buildings destroyed. Each village record gives its location and whether destruction was found. Coverage: western Central African Republic during the 2013 to 2014 conflict. Access: a zipped geodatabase on HDX, created 16 October 2015. Licence: listed on HDX as 'other'; free. Caveats: villages were assessed at different times, so places marked undamaged may have been attacked after their assessment and the number of affected villages may be higher than 125. Simulation uses are observed conflict damage to housing for studies of displacement, reconstruction need and settlement vulnerability, and a validation set for remote-sensing damage detection in rural villages. Related records: the Insecurity Insight incident data and the UNOSAT damage assessments.
name: Western Central African Republic ground and satellite damage assessment of villages, 2013 to 2014 (Human Rights Watch)
provider: Human Rights Watch, published on HDX by OCHA Central African Republic

sources.note: 790 villages, 125 with destruction, over 17,500 buildings, April 2013 to April 2014, caveat on assessment timing, hdx-other
